facts.text: NASA-STD-7009 is NASA's standard for models and simulations, written after the Columbia accident; NASA-HDBK-7009 is its implementation handbook.
facts.quote: NASA-STD-7009 is the US space agency's standard for models and simulations, written after the Columbia accident, and NASA-HDBK-7009 is its implementation handbook.

facts.text: The space shuttle Columbia was lost in 2003; a model was used far outside its data and its warning was then reinterpreted.
facts.quote: After the loss of the space shuttle Columbia in 2003, in which a model was used far outside its data and its warning was then reinterpreted

facts.text: After the Columbia loss, NASA wrote a standard governing how models and simulations must be developed, used and reported when supporting decisions.
facts.quote: NASA wrote a standard for how models and simulations must be developed, used and reported when they support decisions.

facts.text: The passage identifies NASA-STD-7009B as the current version, approved on 5 March 2024.

facts.text: Under NASA-STD-7009, credibility effort must be proportional to the risk of a wrong decision, as set by a criticality assessment.
facts.quote: The credibility effort must be proportional to the risk of a wrong decision, set by a criticality assessment.

facts.text: Under NASA-STD-7009, credibility is rated factor by factor on a 0 to 4 scale, never as a single number.
facts.quote: Credibility is rated factor by factor on a 0 to 4 scale, never as one number.

facts.text: Under NASA-STD-7009, every report to a decision maker must include the best estimate, a statement of uncertainty, the credibility assessment, explicit caveats such as use outside model assumptions or limits, and the risk of accepting the result.
facts.quote: every report to a decision maker must contain a fixed set: the best estimate, a statement of uncertainty, the credibility assessment, explicit caveats such as use outside the model's assumptions or limits, and the risk of accepting the result

facts.text: For the NASA simulation credibility framework, acceptance criteria are defined by the program and approved by technical authority.

facts.text: The booklet treats NASA-STD-7009 as a governance template for an internal board, not as an aviation certification rule or an off-road regulation.

facts.text: The booklet uses the NASA reporting set as one of three layers for the collision mitigation program's validity record.
